title: tomoni.starts - An online training course for elementary school staff on the prevention of mental illness in primary school children
summary:
Background:
More than half of all mental illnesses begin in childhood and adolescence (Jones, 2013; Kessler et al., 2005). Globally, around 13-14% of adolescents are affected by mental illness (UNICEF, 2021), with anxiety disorders, depression, externalizing behavioural disorders (e.g. ADHD, social behaviour disorder) and emotional disorders being particularly common (Polanczyk et al., 2015). Mental illnesses are associated with a lower quality of life and life satisfaction, lower educational status and a higher risk of further psychological and somatic stress for those affected (Schlack et al., 2021). The coronavirus pandemic has increased the risk of mental stress in children and adolescents (Holtmann et al., 2023).

Teachers play a key role in preventing serious illnesses and chronic mental illnesses in children and young people. As gatekeepers, they can recognize and address mental health problems and, if necessary, refer them to an appropriate setting. Due to this responsible task, teachers need sufficient Mental Health Literacy (MHL), which is defined as knowledge and beliefs about mental illness that support their recognition, management or prevention (Jorm et al., 1997). The aim is 1) to increase teachers' ability to act in dealing with mentally distressed pupils and 2) to strengthen teachers' self-confidence in their own ability to act (Whitley et al., 2013). This does not include the diagnosis and treatment of mental disorders, but rather clearly distinguishing between these cases and referring those seeking help to the appropriate professional care systems.

The online teacher training program “tomoni.schools” (see Study 1 and Study 2 registered with the DRKS) was developed by tomoni mental health gGmbH with the aim of preventing mental illness in children and young people. Teachers should learn to recognize possible signs of mental illness and address them in an appreciative manner with their pupils and, if necessary, refer them to further support services. 
tomoni.starts was developed to offer elementary school teachers the opportunity to use an evaluated prevention program. To this end, the content of tomoni.schools was adapted to suit the primary school age of the pupils. tomoni.starts is an online-based training program with a total of eight modules to promote mental health in the primary school context. It is aimed at teachers and other educational staff at elementary school. The aim of the training is to improve the mental health literacy (MHL) of participants - i.e. to expand their knowledge about mental illness, reduce prejudices and strengthen their ability to act when dealing with affected pupils. The program is based on the gatekeeper approach and teaches strategies for early detection, respectful communication and referral to suitable support systems.

Aim of the study:
The aim of the study is to evaluate the medium-term effectiveness of the “tomoni.starts” program.

Overview of the training:
Overall, the tomoni.starts training can be divided into a basic module and 7 specialist modules, each lasting between 1.5 hours and 2 hours. All modules are divided into a part for knowledge transfer and a part for improving skills.  The 7 specialist modules each focus on specific disorders with the highest prevalence at primary school age, as well as a module on parent-teacher conferences. The specialist modules can be attended in any order. Learned strategies are directly applied and practiced in role plays. 
The modules are held by (1) so-called everyday experts who have suffered from mental illness themselves in the past and are at a stable level of functioning in everyday life following therapeutic treatment and (2) experts from academia who have acquired a broad specialist knowledge of mental illness as part of their training and/or employment. This includes students of psychology, psychologists, psychotherapists in training, licensed psychotherapists/child and adolescent psychotherapists, assistant doctors in the field of psychiatry, psychiatrists/child and adolescent psychiatrists or related professional groups.  

Procedure:
After registering online for the study, participants are immediately directed to the first questionnaire, which they complete independently. They are then randomly assigned to either Group 1 or Group 2.
Participants in Group 1 take part in the modules over a period of three months. Three months and six months after completing the modules, they receive a link to the respective online follow-up survey.
Participants in group 2 also receive a link to the respective online questionnaire at these intervals, but do not take part in the modules during the first 3 months. After the surveys, participants in group 2 can take part in the training.

We assume that participation in the programme will improve the self-assessed willingness to act, knowledge about mental illness, the stigmatization of mental illness, confidence in one's own ability to act and general mental health in group 1 of those working in elementary school.

As it has not yet been possible to find a scientifically validated questionnaire for these issues, the working group developed the “Mental Health Literacy and Prevention Survey” (mHELP).
